carrara_marble.doc: White marble with soft grey veins, polished (Perlin's marble: bands of a sine bent by turbulence).

nero_marquina.doc: Black marble crossed by a network of fine white calcite veins, polished (veins along the zero crossings of warped noise).

travertine.doc: Cream travertine, honed: wavy bands of deposition, and pits drawn out along them, dark and hollow.

granite.doc: Pink granite, polished: interlocking crystals of feldspar, quartz and biotite, each its own colour.

slate.doc: Riven slate: dark blue-grey, its cleft face stepped where the cleavage planes break off.

concrete.doc: Cast concrete: grey cement mottled by its mix, flecked with sand and aggregate, and air pores left by the form.

terrazzo.doc: Terrazzo, polished: chips of coloured marble set in a white cement, ground flat.

oak.doc: Varnished oak: growth rings, pale earlywood with its large pores and dark latewood, about a trunk along y (after Liu et al., Simulating the structure and texture of solid wood, 2016).

pine.doc: Pine, matt varnished: pale wood with narrow orange-brown latewood bands, rings wide and wavering.

walnut.doc: Oiled walnut: dark chocolate brown with a wavy figure, and small pores throughout.

brushed_steel.doc: Brushed stainless steel: rough across the brushing (along x) and smooth along it, in fine streaks of Gabor noise.

hammered_copper.doc: Hand-hammered copper: overlapping round dimples, each a little smoother than the metal between them.

rusted_iron.doc: Iron rusting through: patches of flaking orange and brown rust raised over dull, pitted steel.

verdigris_copper.doc: Weathered copper: a pale green patina of verdigris over darkened metal, streaked downwards where rain has run.

galvanized_steel.doc: Hot-dip galvanized steel: zinc spangle, crystals centimetres across, each reflecting with its own roughness.

leather.doc: Brown leather: a pebbled grain of creases between rounded cells, and fine pores, with a soft sheen.

cork.doc: Agglomerated cork: granules of bark pressed together, each its own shade, with dark gaps between.

car_paint.doc: Glossy red car paint with the faint orange-peel waviness of a sprayed clear coat.

linen.doc: Undyed linen: a plain weave of slubby threads a millimetre apart, over and under, in the x-z plane.

terracotta.doc: Unglazed terracotta: fired red clay, mottled where it was fired hotter, with a fine gritty surface.

brick_wall.doc: A wall of red bricks in running bond, each brick its own shade, in recessed grey mortar.

dust.doc: Overlay: a fine pale dust settled on whatever faces up, thickest in corners, over the material given as "over".

grime.doc: Overlay: dark dirt gathered in crevices, corners and where objects meet (found by short rays, the occlusion node), in blotches.

rain_streaks.doc: Overlay: dark streaks where rain has run down steep faces, washed from the edges above, longer than they are wide.

moss.doc: Overlay: cushions of moss on what faces up and in damp hollows, patchy, raised and soft-edged.

lichen.doc: Overlay: crustose lichen, round patches with paler rims spreading over stone, more on faces turned up.

mud_splash.doc: Overlay: mud splashed up from the ground, thick at the foot and spattered above, up to "height" metres.

worn_edges.doc: Overlay: paint ("over") worn through on convex edges and corners to what is under it ("under", bare steel by default), in chipped, ragged patches.

grey_granite.doc: Grey granite, polished: white feldspar, glassy grey quartz and black biotite.

weathered_granite.doc: Granite left outdoors: honed dull, its feldspar chalky, stained with iron, grimy in its hollows and patched with lichen.

black_galaxy.doc: Black granite, polished, flecked with coppery bronzite crystals that glint as it turns.

quartzite.doc: Quartzite, honed: a sugary white rock of fused quartz grains, faintly banded grey and rose, glittering slightly.

engineered_quartz.doc: Engineered quartz worktop: crushed quartz in white resin, polished, speckled grey with tiny mirror flecks.

quartz_crystal.doc: Rock crystal: clear quartz (n = 1.544), clouded by milky veils of inclusions; "tint" makes smoky or rose quartz.

rose_quartz.doc: Rose quartz: quartz crystal tinted pink and mostly milky.

calacatta_marble.doc: Calacatta marble: warm white with bold, wide veins of grey and gold, polished.

verde_marble.doc: Verde Alpi: deep green serpentine marble netted with pale green and white veins, polished.

limestone.doc: Honed limestone: pale cream, faintly mottled, with scattered shell fragments and tiny pores.

basalt.doc: Basalt, sawn: fine-grained dark grey volcanic rock with gas bubbles (vesicles) frozen as round holes.

dried_mud.doc: Dried mud: a crust broken into polygons by shrinkage cracks, the plates curling up at their edges.

asphalt.doc: Asphalt road surface: black bitumen packed with grey and pale stones, worn smooth on top.

glazed_tiles.doc: Glazed ceramic tiles, 15 cm square, each fired a shade between "color" and "color2", in pale grout.

plaster.doc: Hand-trowelled lime plaster: off-white, softly mottled, with the shallow sweeps of the trowel.

weathered_oak.doc: Oak left out for years: silvered grey, its soft earlywood worn back so the grain stands up, split by checks along it.

maple.doc: Curly maple, lacquered: pale creamy wood with faint rings and the rippling flame figure of wavy fibres.

ebony.doc: Ebony, French polished: almost black, with faint brown streaks along the grain.

aged_bronze.doc: Cast bronze aged outdoors: dark brown patina, blackest in its hollows, with bright metal rubbed through on the edges.

cast_iron.doc: Cast iron: dark grey and rough from the sand mould, with a little rust in its hollows.

chipped_paint.doc: Painted steel, chipped: "color" paint flaking off in ragged patches and on its edges, showing rust beneath.

granite_outcrop.doc: Weathered granite as it stands in mountains: grey crystalline rock, mottled and iron-stained, black water streaks down its steep faces, grey crusts and yellow-green map lichen on what faces up; relief from centimetres to metres.

limestone_cliff.doc: A limestone crag: pale grey, ochre where freshly broken, striped black by the cyanobacteria that grow where water runs down it, its steep faces fluted by solution (karren) and its tops pitted.

gneiss.doc: Gneiss: metamorphic rock in folded bands of pale quartz and feldspar and dark biotite, the dark bands weathered back.

schist.doc: Mica schist: silvery grey-green rock of fine wavy foliation, glittering where its mica flakes catch the sun.

scree.doc: Scree: angular stones from fist-sized to a few centimetres, each its own shade, lying on each other with dark gaps between, older stones grown with lichen.

river_gravel.doc: River gravel: rounded pebbles of many rocks (grey, buff, red-brown, white quartz, black) on sand.

dune_sand.doc: Wind-blown sand: ripples ten centimetres apart across the "wind" direction, gentle upwind and steep downwind, darker heavy minerals in their troughs; smooth on slip faces steeper than the sand rests.

beach_sand.doc: A sandy beach: pale dry sand with shell fragments above, dark glossy wet sand with wave ripples below "waterline" metres (scene y).

mudflat.doc: A tidal mudflat or drying lake bed: dark, wet, glossy mud with water standing in its hollows, cracking where it has dried on the rises.

oak_bark.doc: Old oak bark: thick grey-brown ridges split by deep vertical furrows and broken across, green with algae on the side turned from the sun ("shade", a direction).

pine_bark.doc: Scots pine bark low on the trunk: thick grey-brown plates, flaking and reddish where fresh, between deep dark fissures.

birch_bark.doc: Silver birch bark: chalky white with dark horizontal lenticels, peeling to orange in places, black and fissured near the ground (below "rough_below" metres, scene y).

beech_bark.doc: Beech bark: smooth thin grey skin, softly mottled, with pale crusts of lichen and the odd ring of wrinkles.

map_lichen.doc: Overlay: map lichen (Rhizocarpon geographicum), the yellow-green crusts of mountain rock, in round colonies bordered black, broken into tiles by black cracks; on surfaces turned to the sky.

wet.doc: Overlay: wet ground or rock, darker and glossy under a film of water: on a landscape where its wetness says (water gathers in hollows), elsewhere "amount" of it in patches.
